about: The versicle and its response are not two sentences but one psalm verse broken in half: the last verse of Psalm 123, one of the fifteen Gradual Psalms. The priest says the first half, the server the second. The first half has no verb “is” — Latin drops the copula in a nominal sentence, and English has to supply it; the second half carries its own verb, fecit.

s01.narrative: The priest signs himself with the cross — the second time since Mass began. Immediately after, bowing low, he will begin the general confession.

s02.translation: Our help is in the name of the Lord,

w001.function: Nominative: the subject of a sentence that has no verb. Latin need not supply “is”.

w004.function: Ablative after “in” (w003) — the same two words with which the priest began Mass, for he is signing himself again.

w005.function: A genitive depending on “nómine” (w004). The bare form can also be a nominative plural.

w006.function: A relative pronoun whose antecedent is “Dómini” (w005), a genitive: the subject of the second half is picked up from an attribute inside the first, which is why the response cannot stand alone.

w007.function: Perfect: a work done once whose effect stands.
